expected_text_segments:
We think a trading rule earns attention only when its side, costs and comparison are visible.

Our measured-odds series starts with the method. It separates long and short histories and checks trend rows against always long. Euro and yen figures wait for repaired daily closes.

A rising decade can make a long rule look clever. Stop distance and entry choices also change what a historical count means. Construction comparisons describe both sides together.

These are hypothetical historical tests, rather than our trade results or promises about the next trade. The full page sets out the method, its source fingerprint and its limits.

Full analysis: https://capitalchronicle.substack.com/p/how-we-measure-a-trading-rule-before

Capital Chronicle offers analysis only, not financial advice or recommendations.
Capital Chronicle may hold positions in the markets it covers.

media_manifest.caption: Bitcoin daily chart with the native simple averages used by the trend yardstick. Bitstamp via TradingView. The timestamp dates this illustration, not the historical test.
